tagline: Down the old turnpike, from one winter camp to another.
intro: The backway starts on top of Allegheny Mountain, a few miles from the Virginia line, and comes down ten miles of gravel to Bartow on the original bed of the Staunton-Parkersburg Turnpike. It winds through dense forest, past abandoned homesteads and meadows, with views of distant valleys and high ridges.
Both ends were Confederate camps in 1861. The one on top guarded the turnpike's way into the Shenandoah Valley and spent the winter of 1861-62 in snow often knee deep.

moments.title: Camp Allegheny
moments.text: Orders to pull off the mountain had come a few days before the Union attack of December 13, 1861, and once it was beaten back the garrison was kept here all winter.

moments.title: Camp Bartow
moments.text: At the foot of the grade the earthworks of Camp Bartow, attacked by Union troops on October 3, 1861, show best on the hill between the backway and the main highway.

moments.title: Traveller's Repose
moments.text: The private house at the bottom intersection is Traveller's Repose, a well-known inn in the turnpike's 19th-century days.

practical: Gravel the whole way. West Virginia Tourism notes that the road up to Camp Allegheny may be closed by snow in winter, and there may be National Forest fees.
